paragraphs: Friend, here's what this parable teaches: God is patient, and He keeps reaching out. The owner doesn't give up after one servant, so he sends a second, then a third, and then he says, "I will send my beloved son." That's a picture of how far God goes to reach people, and it matters because you are one of the people He's reaching for (Luke 20:10-13).

But the tenants had a problem, and it's one we can all have. They were only renters, and they acted like owners! When they say, "the inheritance will be ours," something has gone sideways (Luke 20:14). Jesus says the owner will come and give the vineyard to others, and the people answer, "May such a thing never happen!" (Luke 20:16).

Then Jesus looks directly at them and says, "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone" (Luke 20:17). Jesus doesn't soften what comes next: "Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed" (Luke 20:18). That's a heavy warning, and it's meant to be taken seriously. So the question for you is a serious one, friend, and the best answer is to build on Him, because that foundation holds, even when your own batch comes out lopsided.
